candidate.title: No Tableau-Randomizing Self-Reduction for Learning Stabilizer with Noise
candidate.subtitle: A barrier the source can exhibit but not close
candidate.one_line: There is no strong, non-trivial tableau-randomizing random self-reduction operator for LSN, for any restriction V and any weight w >= 1.
candidate.status_note: Conjecture 5.20 of the source. It proves a conditional barrier via what it calls the scrambling gap, exhibits an analogous classical no-go, and conjectures the barrier can be made unconditional for tableau-randomizing reductions. It is explicit that this is not an impossibility for random self-reductions in general.
candidate.progress_note: Proved: no random self-reduction from an arbitrary worst-case QNCP instance into LSN, with the obstruction named as exchange symmetry between code and error. Proved conditionally: if the scrambling gap is polynomially related to eps, no number of repeated samples yields a strong non-trivial self-reduction.

parameters.meaning: error rate in the random case; non-trivial means 3/4 - 1/poly(n), since p = 3/4 is always achievable and worthless
the restriction to a set of worst-case Clifford operators
weight bound on the Pauli error

candidate.why_interesting: Classical decoding has a worst-case to average-case self-reduction and the quantum analogue does not; the source turns the reason into a quantitative barrier and names exactly the case it expects to close.
candidate.why_clean: One definition, two named parameters, and an explicit list of the escapes the statement does not cover.

check.notes: Conjecture 5.20 is on page 62 and grounds at 99% coverage; the shortfall is a footnote marker splitting 'defined' across a line break in the text layer, not a wording difference. No repair was needed. The statement records the three escapes the source itself names -- non-tableau-randomizing reductions, dimension-increasing isometries, and eps = 1/poly(n) with smaller p -- because without them a reader would over-read the conjecture as an impossibility for self-reductions generally, which the source explicitly disclaims.
